name: Guizhi Fuling formula (Keishi-bukuryo-gan)
short: Reporting-system study: 1,500 adverse reaction reports, 10 severe; most often stomach upset, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and rash. Trial reviews report mostly mild events.
text: A literature-based post-marketing review of 234 studies of Guizhi Fuling capsules found an adverse event rate of 1.99% when used alone and 8.21% when combined with other drugs, with no severe adverse reactions, and gastrointestinal effects as the most common mild reactions; the authors noted that long-term prospective safety studies are insufficient. An analysis of 1,500 adverse reaction reports from a spontaneous reporting system (2008 to 2017) included 10 severe cases; all patients took the capsules by mouth, the top reactions were gastric dysfunction, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and rash, and 57.4% of reactions began within 24 hours. Meta-analyses of trials, in which the formula was often added to other treatments, found that adding it to low-dose mifepristone for uterine fibroids (28 trials, 2813 patients) did not significantly increase adverse drug reactions; in primary dysmenorrhoea adverse events were generally mild in the four trials that reported safety data, and in 23 trials in prostate diseases no severe adverse effects were reported. In 31 healthy young women, 7 days of the formula decreased the activity of the drug-metabolising enzyme CYP1A2 by 16% but did not alter CYP2D6, CYP3A, xanthine oxidase or NAT2; the abstract does not name any affected medicine.
